To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cyclization of o-pentafluorobenzoic acid having (diene) Fe(CO)3 group gives trans-fused dihydronapthalene, while the cyclization of the corresponding oxime gives trans-fused indole.
O-pentafluorobenzoate oxime having (diene) Fe(CO)3 complex moiety cyclizes by radical chain mechanism and the resulting dihydroindoles undergo facile cis-trans isomerization on acidic silica gel.

the reaction of the (diene)iron complex with O-pentafluorobenzyloxime proceeds via the radical chain mechanism initiated with molecular oxygen, and that the cyclization product undergoes facile isomerization to the cis-fusion isomers on acidic alumina.

the development of novel and efficient methods for the preparation of trans-fused dihydropyrroloindole derivatives, which are important structural motifs found in a number of natural products.
the synthesis and characterization of new transition metal complexes and the application of these complexes in organic synthesis.
the cyclization of oxime having (diene) Fe(CO)3 moieties.

the C-N bond formation is a radical chain reaction and is initiated by the molecular oxygen.
O-pentafluorobenzoate having (diene) Fe(CO)3 group cyclizes to give a dihydroindole, which is easily isomerized to the corresponding cis-fused isomer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the first example of the C-O bond cleavage of oxime having (cyclic diene)Fe(Co)3 moiety, and the first example of cyclization of oxime having such moiety to give dihydroindole.
the C-N bond formation in the cyclization of O-acyloximes proceeds via radical mechanism, and the cyclization of oxime with (cyclooctadiene)Fe2(CO)6 moiety gives cis-fused dihydroisoquinolines.
we have developed the first example of the cyclization reaction of the O-pentafluorobenzoate of the (diene)iron tricarbonyl complex to afford trans-2,3-disubstituted indole.

we have developed an efficient synthetic route to the trans-fused dihydronaphthalene derivatives.
